title: Nasdaq-100 annual reconstitution announced after the close — the once-a-year NDX membership list, plus that quarter's NDX rebalance, both effective at the 2026-12-21 open
source: EST: date derived by applying the index owner's own published methodology to the 2026 calendar, RE-FETCHED AND RE-EXTRACTED THIS SESSION rather than inherited from the proposal or from the 2027 sibling. indexes.nasdaqomx.com/docs/methodology_NDX.pdf, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 422,314 bytes — the same byte count the proposal and the 2027 sibling recorded, which is itself a check that the document has not changed; 29 Flate streams inflated and the text layer rebuilt in-session, then every quote located by whitespace-normalised search because the extracted layer carries kerning-injected spaces). The table carries two schedules at once: 'Reconstitution Frequency: Annually ... Reconstitution Reference Dates: Last trading day of November ... Reconstitution Announcement Dates: After the close on the sixth trading day prior to the Reconstitution Effective Date ... Reconstitution Effective Dates: At market open on the first trading day following the third Friday in December' AND 'Rebalance Frequency: Quarterly ... Rebalance Announcement Dates: After the close on the sixth trading day prior to the Rebalance Effective Date ... Rebalance Effective Dates: At market open on the first trading day following the third Friday in March, June, September, and December' — so in December one announcement carries both, the point the proposal named first. Applied to 2026: December's Fridays are the 4th, 11th, 18th and 25th, the third Friday is 2026-12-18, the effective open is MONDAY 2026-12-21, and the six sessions back from it are 12-18, 12-17, 12-16, 12-15, 12-14 and 12-11 — so the announcement lands after the close on FRIDAY 2026-12-11. No US market holiday falls inside that span (Christmas Day 2026-12-25 is a Friday, after the whole window), so no session is displaced. TWO INDEPENDENT CHECKS RE-COMPUTED THIS SESSION FROM SPY'S OWN SESSION CALENDAR, not inherited: (1) the six-session count back always lands on the SECOND FRIDAY of December, because no US holiday ever falls between the second and third Fridays — 21 of 21 cycles 2005-2025, and December 2026's second Friday is 2026-12-11; (2) the effective-date half of the same rule matches 19 of 19 observed December reconstitutions 2007-2025 (Wikipedia's 'Historical components of the Nasdaq-100' change table, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200, 63,555 bytes — a SECONDARY source, labelled as such). Stays estimate on two counts, not the proposal's three: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no member for an index owner's own published methodology (the same gap every S&P DJI and Russell entry on this calendar records), and Nasdaq's 2026 release does not exist until after the 2026-12-11 close. The proposal's third count — 'a forward application of a standing rule rather than a fetched schedule' — is retired by check (2). The DATE is not in doubt; the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-09), after reading the one proposal for this id in full: proposals/ndx-annual-reconstitution-announcement-2026-12-11.from-sp-quarterly-rebalance-effective-2026-12-21.json, which stands and is now shadowed. This is the NEARER of the calendar's two NDX cycles; the 2027 sibling ndx-annual-reconstitution-announcement-2027-12-10.json was researched the same day and is read in full here. THE OPEN QUESTION THAT SIBLING NAMED IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER REVERSES ONE OF ITS CONCLUSIONS. Its kill switch asked for 'a matched cross-sectional control — similar Nasdaq names not reconstituted, same sessions', and recorded that it needed 'a historical Nasdaq market-cap panel this house does not have'. It does not: rolling the Wikipedia change table backwards from today's 102-ticker roster reconstructs NDX membership for every cycle, and every one of the 117 December removals 2007-2025 is present in the roster the roll-back produces (117/117 — the internal check that the reconstruction is sound). The control is then the CONTINUING members of the same index on the same session: 1,369 usable rows against 82 additions and 73 removals, same family, same size band, same session, same survivorship attrition. THREE RESULTS. (1) THE CONTROL VALIDATES THE BENCHMARK: continuing members' excess over QQQ on the reaction session is -0.023%, 681/1369 negative, sign p=87.1% — a clean null, so QQQ was an unbiased benchmark and the sibling's headline numbers are not an artefact of it. (2) THE REMOVAL EFFECT IS NOT DEAD IN THE MODERN ERA — IT WAS MEASURED AGAINST A NOISIER BASELINE. Demeaning each name by its own cycle's continuing-member mean removes the cycle-common component and sharpens every era: pooled -0.591% at 50/73, sign p=0.2% (vs the sibling's -0.579%, 49/75, p=1.1% against QQQ); 2016-2025 -0.392% at 28/43, p=6.6% (vs -0.271%, p=36.0%); 2019-2025 -0.358% at 22/35, p=17.5% (vs -0.235%, p=73.6%). The sibling's kill switch does not fire — the matched control makes the effect STRONGER, and its 'dead modern' reading softens to 'marginal modern'. At cycle level the two eras' matched diffs are indistinguishable in mean (-0.723% pre-2016 vs -0.716% since, MW p=56.8%) and differ mainly in spread (sd 0.690pp vs 1.823pp, dispersion MW p=12.1% — suggestive, underpowered at 19 cycles). (3) THE ADDITION LEG IS STILL A NULL ON THE MATCHED CONTROL: demeaned -0.004%, 45/82, sign p=44.0%, and 0 of 19 cycle means reached the S&P panel's +2.31% (max +1.358%). AND THE SIBLING'S ONE LIVE NUMBER IS ROUGHLY HALVED BY THE RIGHT BASELINE: continuing NDX members themselves print a 1.924x median relative turnover on the implementation Friday (1282/1368 above 1.0x), because that session is quadruple witching. The index-flow-specific part is the RATIO — cohort over continuing members, median 2.403x, minimum 1.419x, 18 of 19 cycles at or above 1.5x — not the 4.9x-versus-QQQ's-1.30x level. Same on the reaction session: cohort 1.27x against continuing members' 1.047x (MW p=0.0%), a real footprint about half its apparent size. A HYPOTHESIS FOR THE NEXT LANE, HELD AS ONE: the matched removal diff is negative in 9 of 9 low-VIX cycles (announcement-session VIX <= 17.61, mean -1.315%, sign p=0.4%) against 6 of 9 high-VIX cycles (mean -0.259%, p=50.8%), and the pre-2016 era is the high-VIX one (mean VIX 24.60 vs 16.23, MW p=3.4%) — so era and volatility regime are confounded in the OPPOSITE direction from the decay story. The direct low-versus-high test is only MW p=21.4%, so this is a question, not a finding. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: any membership names, which do not exist until Nasdaq publishes after the 2026-12-11 close; that any of this is tradeable — the one live price effect is short-side and the house-wide short ban blocks it, it does not extend past the reaction session, and no house playbook is index-flow-keyed (trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md re-grepped this session for rebalanc|index effect|index inclusion|reconstitut|deletion|witching|closing auction|index flow, zero hits in both). WHAT IS SPECIFIC TO 2026: the corridor is 27 tracked ids within five days, against 4 for the 2027 sibling, and 2026-12-11 itself carries four more — government-funding-deadline-2026-12-11 and cr-expiry-2026-12-11 (both high), russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11 (medium) and sp-rebalance-reference-close-2026-12-11 — with fomc-2026-12-09 at T-2 and cpi-2026-12-10 at T-1. Any index-level tape reading of this session belongs to fiscal news, not index flow, which is exactly why this ledger's own forward tests score on cohort-versus-continuing cross-sections rather than on the session. Low impact and market-structure only; estimate; nothing here licenses an entry. Ledger: docs/research/events/ndx-annual-reconstitution-announcement-2026-12-11.md
